items.title: Directory-based access for OpenSharing SecureConnect (Public Preview)
items.text: OpenSharing SecureConnect can now deliver eligible tables and views to Azure Databricks recipients using serverless compute with directory-based access instead of per-file pre-signed URLs, for better performance. This feature is in Public Preview. Account admins can manage the OpenSharing SecureConnect Directory Based Access preview from the account console Previews page. See Directory-based access for SecureConnect.

items.title: Latest automatic expiration date for legacy OpenSharing open recipient tokens moved to February 25, 2027
items.text: OpenSharing open recipient tokens issued before February 25, 2026, with expiration dates after February 25, 2027, or with no expiration date, now automatically expire on February 25, 2027, instead of December 8, 2026. Data providers should rotate these tokens before February 25, 2027, to avoid breaking changes. Rotated tokens use the new recipient-specific URL format. See Changes to OpenSharing (formerly Delta Sharing) open recipient tokens.

items.title: Recipient-specific URLs for OpenSharing open recipients
items.text: In most regions, OpenSharing open recipients now use a recipient-specific URL that includes the recipient ID in the host name. Bearer tokens created or rotated since September 2026 use the new URL, and the OpenSharing UI shows the new URL for OpenID Connect (OIDC) federation recipients. Recipients can allow egress to their recipient-specific host name instead of the shared regional host name. Existing URLs and tokens continue to work until they expire. See Changes to OpenSharing (formerly Delta Sharing) open recipient tokens.

items.text: Artifact Registry is now generally available. Store container images as governed assets in Unity Catalog, browse images and versions in Catalog Explorer, list and manage images with the databricks software-artifacts Databricks CLI commands, and delete images through the Software Artifacts API. See Artifact Registry.

items.id: November_25_2026#Deprecated: The BigQuery Storage API v1beta1 is deprecated and will be shut down on August 31, 2027.
items.title: The BigQuery Storage API v1beta1 is deprecated and will be shut down on August 31, 2027
items.text: The BigQuery Storage API v1beta1 is deprecated and will be shut down on August 31, 2027. Key milestone dates: Nov 20, 2026: Access to the BigQuery Storage API v1beta1 is restricted to projects that recorded active usage between March 1, 2026, and August 31, 2026. August 31, 2027: The BigQuery Storage API v1beta1 will be fully shut down. After this date, calls to the v1beta1 endpoint will fail with a NOT_FOUND error. What you need to do: To prevent service disruption, migrate your workloads from v1beta1 to the generally available BigQuery Storage API v1. The v1 API is backward-compatible with v1beta1. SDKs and connectors: If you use connectors or client libraries, update them to the latest versions to ensure they default to the v1 API: Simba ODBC/JDBC for BigQuery Google BigQuery ODBC / JDBC driver Trino BigQuery plugin Apache Beam BigQuery connector Spark BigQuery connector Scio BigQuery plugin Custom code: If your applications call the v1beta1 API directly (for example, using gRPC),…

items.id: November_24_2026#Feature: The following table-valued functions are now generally available (GA) in the query editor and as part of conversational analytics to help you analyze your data:
items.title: The following table-valued functions are now generally available (GA) in the query editor and as part of conversational analytics to help you analyze your data (GA)
items.text: The following table-valued functions are now generally available (GA) in the query editor and as part of conversational analytics to help you analyze your data: ML.TREND: identify the directional trajectory of your data. ML.SEASONALITY: identify repeating patterns in your data. ML.DETECT_CHANGE_POINTS: identify intervals where structural shifts occur in your data. ML.CORRELATION: identify the statistical correlation between a target column and one or more metric columns.

items.id: November_23_2026#Feature: Version 1.1 of the TabFM model is now available as the default model for the AI.PREDICT and AI.EVALUATE functions.
items.title: Version 1.1 of the TabFM model is now available as the default model for the AI.PREDICT and AI.EVALUATE functions (Preview)
items.text: Version 1.1 of the TabFM model is now available as the default model for the AI.PREDICT and AI.EVALUATE functions. Version 1.1 expands input limits to 80,000 sampled training rows (up from 10,000) and 128 feature columns (up from 50). This model reduces latency by up to 50x—interactive queries return predictions in around 1 second, and you can score millions of rows in a single BigQuery job. This feature is in Preview.
